application_type_generation.citation: plantuml.com/command-line, 'Output Format' table (exhaustive list: eps, html, latex, pdf, png, scxml, svg, txt, utxt, braille — all diagram/image or diagram-adjacent markup formats, none of them application source code); corroborated by zero GitHub code/issue search hits for 'pydantic' or 'sqlalchemy' in plantuml/plantuml
application_type_generation.rationale: PlantUML is a rendering engine: every documented output format is a diagram representation (raster image, vector image, or diagram-description markup like SCXML for state machines). None of the ten enumerated formats produces application source code (no Pydantic models, SQLAlchemy mappings, dataclasses, or any other language binding). This is the honest negative the assignment asked to record explicitly rather than leave implicit: PlantUML has no application-type generator of any kind for ER/IE/Chen diagrams, consistent with its purpose as a renderer rather than a schema compiler.

physical_ddl_derivation.rationale: Per the brief's own instruction, DDL derivation is recorded as not-applicable rather than not-expressible whenever no type-generation capability exists to build it on top of. Since PlantUML has no application-type generator (see above), and no SQL/DDL-specific output format appears anywhere in the Output Format table either, DDL derivation from a PlantUML ER/IE source is recorded as not-applicable.
